ideas.description: Built on the first feasible airbench96-style base (I001/I003 knee). Make one systems change and leave the recipe alone. Move the whole training step into one torch.compile'd function: forward, backward, Nesterov SGD update and lookahead blend. Apply the update with torch._foreach_* ops (or SGD foreach/fused=True) so there is no per-parameter Python loop. Pass lr and the lookahead schedule as 0-d GPU tensors so changing them never triggers a recompile. Compile and warm up this function in build() on synthetic data, covering the full batch and the final partial batch. Keep the epoch count, seeds, lr, wd, LS and widths identical to the base.
ideas.expected: Time drops about 5-10% against the base at the same epoch count, because Python and kernel-launch overhead is a noticeable share of a run near 10 s. Accuracy stays within 0.2 pp of the base, so feasibility is unchanged. If the gain is under 3%, the step was not launch-bound and H2.2 loses support.

drop.reason: It duplicates I003, which already includes an epoch sweep that adapts to the I001 result (9, or 11 if 10 misses). Running a separate fixed 8.5-epoch point before the knee is known spends a run on a point that is probably infeasible. The H1.1.2 TTA-gap question can be answered from the fitted accuracy-vs-epochs curve from I001/I003. A point at about 8.5 epochs can be added later if that fit leaves it ambiguous.

structured_output.summary: Only the stub baseline has run so far (E000: 0.012 accuracy, 0.11 s), so no hypothesis is settled yet and the queue was already full at 8. I dropped I002 because the I003 epoch sweep already covers it and adapts to the I001 result. I added one exploit idea for H2.2.1, which had no test yet: a single compiled training step with a foreach/fused optimizer and lookahead update, lr passed as tensors to avoid recompiles, and warmup in build(). The queue now holds 8 ideas: I001 (base recipe, priority 5); I003 (find the knee, 4); I004 (noise floor, 3); I005 (label smoothing 0.2 vs 0.3, 3); the new H2.2.1 idea (3); I006 (lookahead ablation, 2); I007 (Muon, explore, 2); and I008 (progressive resizing, explore, 2). That is roughly 2/3 exploit and 1/3 explore. Three hypotheses still have no idea queued. H1.5.1 (512 vs 576 width) and H2.1.1 (eager vs compiled ablation) are left until a feasible base exists, and H1.4.1 (hard-example selection) is left until the knee is known. Because I001 has not run yet, its compile and warmup must cover every shape. If it misses 0.753, I003 should run 11 epochs before any ablation.
